handoff.purpose: Derive and measure candidate correctness tasks from git commits; provide a gate for task attempts.

symbols.name: _test_functions
symbols.note: Parses a Python file with ast and returns a dict mapping pytest node-id suffixes to source segments for test functions/methods.

symbols.name: derive_task_from_commit
symbols.note: Proposes a candidate task dict from a commit's diff, using added/changed tests as FAIL_TO_PASS and unchanged as PASS_TO_PASS.

symbols.name: seed_task_from_commit
symbols.note: Measures candidate node ids in a disposable worktree, admits only verified nodes, returns task and diagnostics.

symbols.name: correctness_gate
symbols.note: Returns a gate callable that fails closed on unverified tasks or moved selections.

claims.text: The key is the node id form pytest actually accepts -- ``test_x`` for a module-level function, ``ClassName::test_x`` for a method -- because the class qualifier is not optional and getting it wrong makes the node id ``missing``.
claims.why: The code produces module-level functions as bare names and class methods as ClassName::method.

claims.text: That is not a hypothetical: the first run of this seeder used unqualified names from ``structcore.extract_units`` (which reports a method as a bare ``test_alive_then_stale``) and the before-state check refuted 19 of 22 candidate nodes in one commit for exactly that reason.
claims.why: The historical incident is not present in this chunk; the code's behavior is consistent with the claim but the event itself is not observable here.

claims.text: ``ast`` rather than a regex or the structural extractor: it is stdlib, it is exact about nesting, and pytest node ids are a Python-only concept anyway.
claims.why: The function imports ast and uses it for parsing and nesting.

claims.text: A file that does not parse contributes nothing (the caller then mints nothing from it) rather than contributing guesses.

The commit's own diff is the oracle, exactly as in ``mint.py``: what the commit ADDED or CHANGED in a test file is a FAIL_TO_PASS candidate, what it left untouched in the same file is a PASS_TO_PASS candidate, and the base is the commit's parent.
claims.why: The code compares before/after blobs of changed test files; changed units go to f2p, unchanged to p2p; base is sha^.

claims.text: NOTHING here is trusted. Every derived node id is a CLAIM that :func:`verify_before_state` then tries to refute by running it on the base; a node id this function gets wrong (a test nested in a class, say, whose real node id carries the class) comes back ``missing`` and takes the task down with it.
claims.why: verify_before_state is not in this chunk; the claim about its behavior cannot be checked here.

claims.text: Returns ``None`` when the commit changed no test file -- a real and common case (``efd0ed6`` in this repo's own history is a fix with no test at all), reported by returning nothing rather than by inventing a label.
claims.why: The function returns None when no f2p candidates are found (which happens when no test file changed or no added/changed test units exist). The historical sha is not verifiable here.

claims.text: THE LISTS ARE MEASURED, NEVER CLAIMED. :func:`derive_task_from_commit` proposes node ids off the commit's diff; every one of them is a guess, and this function's whole job is to try to refute each guess by running it twice in one disposable worktree: base + test overlay -> the BEFORE statuses; base + test overlay + reference fix -> the AFTER statuses
claims.why: The code runs before_run on base+overlay and after_run after applying the reference patch.

claims.text: FAIL_TO_PASS not passing BEFORE, passing AFTER, and TOUCHED by the commit (a test that was already red and that the commit never mentions is not this fix's witness)
claims.why: The admission logic requires before_status in PROVEN_NOT_PASSING, after_status == STATUS_PASSED, and node in changed.

claims.text: PASS_TO_PASS passing BEFORE and passing AFTER
claims.why: The code appends node to p2p when both statuses are STATUS_PASSED.

claims.text: Everything else is DROPPED WITH ITS REASON RECORDED on the task (``dropped_candidates``) -- never silently, because the drop rate is itself the measurement of how much a corpus is worth.
claims.why: The code records each drop reason in diagnostics['dropped'] and copies it to task['dropped_candidates'].

claims.text: Real examples from this repo's own history, both found by running this rather than by reasoning: a test named ``..._still_...`` that the fix ADDED but which already passed on the base (demoted to the regression set), and an ``xfail``-marked test that is red before AND after the reference fix, so it can never witness anything (dropped).
claims.why: The examples are historical and not in this chunk; the code's logic does handle both cases (a passed-before added test goes to p2p via the first branch; a red-before-red-after test is dropped by the last elif).

claims.text: A task with no surviving FAIL_TO_PASS node is NOT admitted -- ``(None, diagnostics)`` with the reason. ``efd0ed6`` in this repo is such a commit: a real fix that shipped no test at all.
claims.why: The code returns None with a reason when f2p is empty. The historical sha is not verifiable here.

claims.text: IT FAILS CLOSED ON AN UNVERIFIED TASK, and that is the point. The attempt's worktree already HAS the candidate's change in it by the time a gate runs, so the before-state cannot be measured there -- it has to have been measured earlier, against this exact base revision. A task with no verified before-state receipt for ``ctx.base_revision`` is REFUSED (``passed=False``) rather than evaluated, because a FAIL_TO_PASS list that was never shown to fail is precisely the vacuous green this module exists to prevent.
claims.why: The gate's inner logic that checks ctx.base_revision and the receipt is not shown in this chunk; only the initial setup and verdict helper are present.

claims.text: IT ALSO REFUSES A SELECTION THAT MOVED. The receipt records the digest of the selection it was measured under; this recomputes that digest from the task as presented and refuses on any mismatch. Widening the lists after the verification (say, to include a test the candidate itself added), narrowing them to drop an inconvenient one, or pointing them at a different base all change the digest and all get the same refusal. What was measured is what was declared, checkably.
claims.why: The digest recomputation and refusal logic is not in this chunk; it is in the remainder of the _gate function.

claims.text: What this gate adds over ``spine.attempt.pytest_gate``: pytest_gate asks "did the suite exit 0", which a candidate satisfies by changing nothing. This asks "did the previously-RED tests go GREEN, and did the previously-GREEN ones stay green" -- a question a no-op change cannot pass.
claims.why: The comparison with spine.attempt.pytest_gate is not in this chunk; the gate's actual checks are not visible here.
